fact: Africa Data Protection reports that a decree of 8 June 2026 abolished Niger's Haute Autorite de protection des donnees a caractere personnel (HAPDP), that an ordonnance of the same day repealed the 2022 law's provisions founding it, and that its tasks pass to the Justice and Interior ministries.

Niger's President signed a decree on 8 June 2026 abolishing the Haute Autorité de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (HAPDP), ending its officials' functions from signature and transferring its missions to the Ministry of Justice and the Ministry of the Interior, per the Secretariat General of Government communique.
Iro Adamou, named member and president of the HAPDP by decree 4016/P/CNSP of 24 June 2024, took the oath before the Cour d'Etat on 18 September 2024, per Le Sahel.
